predecessors.name: Cisalpine Republic
predecessors.text: 'the same areas that had comprised the Cisalpine Republic, primarily Lombardy and Romagna' (12 departments, more than 42,500 km2)

successors.name: Austrian Empire
successors.text: 'the remains of the kingdom were annexed by the Austrian Empire as the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia'

ledger.x: 26 January 1802: the Cisalpine Republic becomes the Italian Republic at the Lyon meetings.
17 March 1805: the Republic becomes the Kingdom of Italy.
1806: the Venetian lands join the Kingdom.
8 May 1809: the Austrians are driven out of Italy.
10 June 1810: South Tyrol joins the Kingdom.
10 June 1810: Istria and Dalmatia go to France.
11 April 1814: Napoleon abdicates the throne of Italy.

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition
wars.outcome: French victory; the Peace of Pressburg (26 December 1805) gave the Kingdom of Italy Venetia, Istria and Dalmatia.

wars.name: War of the Fifth Coalition
wars.outcome: Austria's invasion of Italy under Archduke John was beaten at the Piave on 8 May 1809 and he was forced out of Italy; Schönbrunn (14 October 1809) then exchanged Istria, Dalmatia and Ragusa for South Tyrol.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: Napoleon's abdication (11 April 1814), Eugène's surrender (23 April) and the Austrian occupation of Milan (28 April) ended the Kingdom, annexed by Austria as the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia.

certainty.note: The pages name departments and treaties, not boundary lines; the Venetian, Istrian and Dalmatian lines and the 1808 and 1810 additions are approximate regions, and Dalmatia was 'never fully incorporated'.
